caption: A 7-segment display: four input lines (a 4-bit number) light the seven lamps of a readable digit on its front face, 0-9 then A b C d E F, with no flicker while the number changes (glitch-free). A chain of subtract comparators turns the four bits into one signal strength; four shared dust rulers give every threshold (two segments per ruler where they fit); each run of values a segment lights is one subtract comparator between two taps of the same ruler; routed repeater lanes carry each segment to its lamp, with the inputs' delays equalised so every change arrives in the same tick. Catalog parts: comparator gates, repeater delays.

Glitch-free and safe from dropped items: clk-item's ring stacks (a subtract-comparator chain turns the 4 bits into one signal strength s; per segment a ring of window comparators lights its lamp through a repeater lane), with ring a's line moved east of its rear hopper so ring g's window contacts switch race-free, rings b, c and d computing their segment's complement (their lanes, a repeater, a torch and a repeater, filter both short pulses and dips), and the window constants in chests and shulker boxes instead of hoppers (nothing picks up a dropped item).
